NAME: 7-Day Rolling Revenue per Store
DESC:
A retail chain wants to smooth its daily sales curves. For every store and every day with sales, compute the revenue over the last 7 calendar days.

Input

sales_df

column type description
store_id string never null
sale_date date never null
amount double sale amount; may be null

A store can have several rows on the same day, and no row at all on some days.

Rules

  1. Rows with a null amount are ignored. A (store, day) appears in the output only if the store has at least one row with a non-null amount on that day.
  2. daily_revenue is the sum of the amounts of the store on that day.
  3. The 7-day window of day D covers the calendar days from D - 6 to D, both inclusive, whatever the number of days with sales in between.
  4. rolling_7d_revenue is the sum of daily_revenue over the window. rolling_7d_avg is rolling_7d_revenue / 7 (always divided by 7 calendar days).
  5. days_with_sales_7d is the number of days of the window that appear in the output for this store.
  6. All doubles are rounded to 2 decimals.

Output

One row per (store, day with sales), with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
store_id string
sale_date date
daily_revenue double
rolling_7d_revenue double
rolling_7d_avg double
days_with_sales_7d long

Rows are sorted by store_id ascending, then sale_date ascending.

Example

sales_df

store_id sale_date amount
A 2024-03-01 100.0
A 2024-03-01 50.0
A 2024-03-02 null
A 2024-03-03 30.0
A 2024-03-07 20.0
B 2024-03-05 7.5
A 2024-03-08 10.0
A 2024-03-10 5.0

Expected output

store_id sale_date daily_revenue rolling_7d_revenue rolling_7d_avg days_with_sales_7d
A 2024-03-01 150.0 150.0 21.43 1
A 2024-03-03 30.0 180.0 25.71 2
A 2024-03-07 20.0 200.0 28.57 3
A 2024-03-08 10.0 60.0 8.57 3
A 2024-03-10 5.0 35.0 5.0 3
B 2024-03-05 7.5 7.5 1.07 1

On 2024-03-08 the window covers 2024-03-02 to 2024-03-08, so the sales of 2024-03-01 are no longer included.

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(sales_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas, do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve, do not use Python UDFs.
  • sales_df has up to 10^7 rows, for up to 10^4 stores.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(sales_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Une ligne par (magasin, jour) : montants null ignorés, jour sans montant réel => pas de ligne.
    daily = (
        sales_df
        .filter(F.col("amount").isNotNull())
        .groupBy("store_id", "sale_date")
        .agg(F.sum("amount").alias("daily"))
    )

    # 2. Fenêtre en jours CALENDAIRES : rangeBetween sur un entier "numéro de jour".
    #    (rangeBetween directement sur une colonne date est refusé par Spark.)
    day_num = F.datediff(F.col("sale_date"), F.lit("1970-01-01"))
    w = Window.partitionBy("store_id").orderBy(day_num).rangeBetween(-6, 0)   # [J-6, J] = 7 jours

    rolling = F.sum("daily").over(w)
    result = daily.select(
        "store_id",
        "sale_date",
        F.round("daily", 2).alias("daily_revenue"),
        F.round(rolling, 2).alias("rolling_7d_revenue"),
        F.round(rolling / 7, 2).alias("rolling_7d_avg"),          # divisé par 7 jours, pas par le nb de lignes
        F.count(F.lit(1)).over(w).alias("days_with_sales_7d"),
    )
    return result.orderBy("store_id", "sale_date")
